identity.name: Potassium citrates
identity.chemical_class: Potassium salts of citric acid (citrate salts)

function.mechanism: Buffers food pH and chelates metal ions, improving stability and formulation performance.
common_food_categories: acidified and buffered foods and beverages
formulations requiring pH control under GMP

adi.basis: EU food additives database entry for E332 reports ADI as 'Not specified' and cites EFSA/SCF evaluations.

efsa.key_finding: Accessible EU/EFSA-linked records indicate non-numerical ADI (not specified) for E332 and continued authorization.

fda.notes: Affirmed as GRAS for direct human food use; permitted under current good manufacturing practice as sequestrant, pH control agent, stabilizer, and emulsifier.

adi.basis: JECFA lists ADI as 'Not limited' for potassium dihydrogen citrate (INS 332(i)) and potassium citrate (INS 332(ii)).

concerns.summary: Randomized clinical evidence indicates oral potassium loading (including potassium citrate) can raise plasma potassium more in CKD and may increase hyperkalemia risk in susceptible patients.

no_concern_confirmed: EU E332 entry reports ADI not specified
JECFA ADI is not limited for INS 332(i)/(ii)
FDA affirms potassium citrate as GRAS in 21 CFR 184.1625
No explicit IARC monograph classification entry identified for potassium citrate

adi_exceedance.notes: A numerical ADI is not set (EFSA not specified; JECFA not limited), so risk management is driven more by potassium-handling vulnerability than ADI exceedance calculations.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory consensus indicates low concern at normal food-additive exposure (EU authorized, FDA GRAS, JECFA not limited). However, clinical evidence shows a credible renal/potassium-handling caveat in vulnerable populations (especially CKD) under higher oral potassium loads.
key_factors: EU entry: ADI not specified for E332
JECFA ADI not limited for INS 332(i)/(ii)
CKD-focused RCT evidence of higher hyperkalemia susceptibility with oral potassium loading
